title: The base change maps of two side by side cartesian squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes whose two squares are cartesian, with f and h as well as f' and h' Tor independent, the lemma asserts that the base change maps of equation labelled equation-base-change-map for the two squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle (statement lines 1374-1389). The proof notes that then f and h o h' are Tor independent, so the statement makes sense, marking that step 'details omitted', and introduces the adjoints a, a', a'' for f, f', f'' together with the arrows gamma_right, gamma_left and gamma_rect written through the inverses of the isomorphisms xi_right, xi_left and xi_rect, which are the duals of the corresponding ordinary base change maps, and the canonical maps 1 -> h_* h^* and g^* g_* -> 1 (proof lines 1391-1418). Using k = g o g' and m = h o h', hence k^* = (g')^* o g^* and m^* = (h')^* o h^*, the claim is that gamma_rect equals gamma_left o gamma_right (proof lines 1420-1430). The proof contemplates a large diagram whose right hand side is that composition and whose left hand side is gamma_rect; all quadrilaterals on the right commute by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats or the discussion before Categories, Definition labelled categories-definition-horizontal-composition, so it suffices to prove that the composition g_* o (g')_* o a'' -> g_* o a' o (h')_* -> a o h_* o (h')_* through xi_left and xi_right equals xi_rect, which is the statement dual to Cohomology, Remark labelled cohomology-remark-compose-base-change-horizontal (proof lines 1432-1468). Organising the diagram chase so that only the dual of the known horizontal composition of ordinary base change maps remains is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
